messages.content:
You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.
Cast marked hasForm: false have no body and are never drawn. Describe only the shared place, weather and light. Where the section shows one of them, its presence may appear only as smoke, cloud, fire, wind or light spread through the place. Never describe its throne, seat, chariot, robe, train, face, hands, hair, body or silhouette, even as an empty seat, a denial or a figure made of light: bodily words in the text are metaphors. Keep formed characters' own situational clothing and props attached to them. The cast list covers the whole section; do not force every cast member into the shared setting or add individual poses, actions or moments.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Creation and the patriarchs. People: Ancient Near Eastern households, herders and farmers. Dress: Simple wool or linen wraps, tunics and sandals. Buildings and objects: Wild land, tents, wells, altars and mud-brick towns as the text allows.

timeOfDay.description: The time of day or change in time across the section. At most 200 characters.

weather.description: Shared environmental conditions, without bodily metaphors. At most 200 characters.

light.description: Situational illumination shared by the section. A no-form subject's presence may appear only as light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind spread through the place, never as a shape or figure. At most 200 characters.

clothing.description: Only formed characters' situational clothing and shared props, never a no-form subject's clothing, even as a denial. At most 200 characters.

messages.content:
You check an illustration plan before it is drawn. You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.
The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.
Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.
- outside_instant: a selected or described person or presence does not belong in this moment, such as a speaker, writer, prophet or listener put into a scene their words only describe or made a figure of their own words, the narrator of a story or vision, someone from a different event, or a no-form presence the moment does not show. Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.
- look_conflict: an OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS value (only when supplied) contradicts the scene, the text or the depiction rules. Quote that value.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts a selected entry's fixed canon. Quote the scene field.
- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.
For each problem, copy a short exact phrase from a scene field or a selected id into planQuote (from an owner constraint for look_conflict) and give a one-sentence reason.

You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.
The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.
Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.
- outside_instant: a selected or described person or presence does not belong in this moment, such as a speaker, writer, prophet or listener put into a scene their words only describe or made a figure of their own words, the narrator of a story or vision, someone from a different event, or a no-form presence the moment does not show. Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.
- look_conflict: an OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS value (only when supplied) contradicts the scene, the text or the depiction rules. Quote that value.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts a selected entry's fixed canon. Quote the scene field.
- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.
For each problem, copy a short exact phrase from a scene field or a selected id into planQuote (from an owner constraint for look_conflict) and give a one-sentence reason.

- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Abram, later Abraham: an elderly man of seventy-five to one hundred years and beyond; lean, weathered build from years of travel; dark skin tanned by desert sun; short greying beard and hair; deep-set, steady eyes and lined face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed wool wrap over a earth-brown linen tunic, leather sandals. Signature prop: a long wooden herder's staff.
- Isaac: a young man in late youth to middle age; lean, sturdy build from herding and labour in the open country; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut close at the neck, short beard kept trim; calm, steady face with heavy-lidded, grey-brown eyes that grow dim with age; wears a plain undyed linen tunic with a woollen wrap of earth-brown ochre, and leather sandals; carries a wooden staff of plain olive wood, and a bundle of kindling when bound to the wood at Moriah.
- Mount Moriah: a rocky ridge of pale limestone rising above a dry upland plain, with terraced slopes of scrub, wild thyme, and scattered terebinth trees. On the summit a bare stone outcrop serves as an altar place, with a low ring of unhewn stones. Distant hills fold away in dusty blue haze.

Primary subject: Abraham, arm raised, knife gripped in his hand, bending over the altar
Action: Abraham is about to strike, the blade poised at the moment before the angel's call
Setting: Rocky ridge of Moriah with scrub, an altar of stacked stones, wood laid in ranks
Secondary elements: Isaac bound and laid on the wood, firewood bundled on the ground, a lone tent and well at the foot of the slope
Mood: Grave, tense, sorrowful and reverent
Time of day: Early morning sun rising over the ridge, clear dry still air

Palette: Transparent washes of ochre, sienna, indigo and sage covering the whole picture, sky and corners included.
Lighting: Clear natural light; shadows as cool layered washes.
Materials and texture: Confident ink linework, wet-in-wet blooms and granulating pigment within the depicted world.
Composition: A complete scene: setting, sky and ground painted out to every edge and corner, with detail concentrated on key subjects.

1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Leviticus 11:7: "The pig, because it has a split hoof, and is cloven-footed, but doesn’t chew the cud, is unclean to you."

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement
People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples.
Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments.
Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.
Technology: Bronze tools, chariots and early iron; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Moses; Aaron, brother of Moses

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.
- Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.
- the camp of Israel: a wide wilderness encampment of dun-coloured tents of woven goat-hair cloth in ordered rows, with a central sanctuary tent and a gate; bare stony desert plain, scattered acacia and tamarisk, distant dark mountain slopes; a pillar of cloud above the camp by day and fire by night; ash-pits and a clean place beyond its edges.
- Only Moses, Aaron, brother of Moses, the camp of Israel have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Moses standing upright, one arm raised toward the pig at the camp's edge
Action: Moses gestures toward a pig in the scrub while Aaron stands attentive beside him
Setting: Edge of the Israelite camp in the wilderness, tent cords, rough stone and dry scrub
Secondary elements: A pig with cloven hooves rooting near the tents, a crowd of Israelites in woven tunics and cloaks gathered in a loose ring, faint radiant cloud glowing above the tabernacle
Mood: Solemn, attentive and grounded
Time of day: Midday, clear dry air with pale haze and a faint hot wind
Composition: Wide view from the side, Moses and Aaron in the foreground left, the pig and gathered people spread across the middle ground, tabernacle and distant hills behind

ART STYLE: Classical
Rendering: Stylized, painterly, mysterious and expansive. The painterly treatment belongs to the depicted world itself, not to a photographed physical artwork.
Negatives: Avoid photorealism or a photographic look. Avoid childish/cartoonish styling. Never present the scene as a painting on a wall, gallery piece, framed artwork, fresco, mural, poster, manuscript page, or printed illustration. Do not show canvas texture, paper edges, matting, border, mockup, or surrounding room. The depicted world must fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Mature, grounded color; rich but restrained contrast.
Lighting: Luminous, dramatic lighting.
Materials and texture: Gritty, raw texture; avoid polished digital smoothness.
Composition: Cinematic, immersive viewpoint; heroic but grounded.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject, landscape and layout.
- Image 2: Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: The hare, because it chews the cud but doesn’t have a parted hoof, is unclean to you.
- After: You shall not eat their meat. You shall not touch their carcasses. They are unclean to you.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, described by the scene plan below.

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: the presence has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement
People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples.
Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments.
Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.
Technology: Bronze tools, chariots and early iron; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Moses; The Israelite people (the children of Israel)

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.
- The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.
- Red Sea: a wide, deep arm of open water between desert shores, its surface dark blue-green under wind. Sand dunes and low reddish cliffs line the coast; scattered tamarisk and palms grow at the water's edge. Bare rock outcrops and shallow wadis run down to the shore, and a distant fortified town sits on the northern ridge.
- Only Moses, The Israelite people (the children of Israel), Red Sea have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Moses at the water's edge, arm extended low over the parting sea, plain cloak and staff in his other hand.
Action: The east wind blows the sea back, exposing dry ground at the bottom while the waters stand piled up on either side.
Setting: Open shore of the Red Sea with wind-scoured sand, rocky wilderness hills behind and dry sea floor between two walls of water.
Secondary elements: Israelites in woven tunics and cloaks gathered on the shore behind Moses, watching; sand and spray lifted by the wind; pillar of cloud and fire glowing faintly above the camp, its radiance falling across the parted waters.
Mood: Awe, tense expectancy and quiet faith, with grief and hope held together.
Time of day: Deep night turning toward dawn, dark cloud banks breaking open, strong east wind.
Composition: Wide view from the shore looking out over the parting sea, Moses in the foreground near the left edge, the people at the shore and the exposed sea floor leading the eye toward the far water.

ART STYLE: Ink & Watercolor
Rendering: Pen-and-ink drawing with transparent watercolor washes laid over the whole picture; a finished watercolor painting of the work's world, not a sketch.
Negatives: Washes, pigment and scenery must reach every edge. No white or cream paper margins, unpainted corners, paper edges, sketchbook, tape, border or vignette. Do not present the scene on a sheet of paper or against a blank backdrop. Avoid photorealism, digital airbrush smoothness and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Transparent washes of ochre, sienna, indigo and sage covering the whole picture, sky and corners included.
Lighting: Clear natural light; shadows as cool layered washes.
Materials and texture: Confident ink linework, wet-in-wet blooms and granulating pigment within the depicted world.
Composition: A complete scene: setting, sky and ground painted out to every edge and corner, with detail concentrated on key subjects.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.

You plan one illustration of one moment of a work's text. You get the moment with its neighbours in the same story section, the work brief, the era, the section cast and a SECTION LOOK GUIDE. Return only JSON.
- Draw one scene at one instant: no collage and no sequence of steps. If the moment recounts several actions, pick one representative instant. If it has no event (a list, genealogy, law, saying or greeting), illustrate its content or setting through people, places and things, never as a written document.
- Show what the moment is about. When the moment is mostly someone's words (a prophecy, oracle, poem, proverb, prayer, letter, argument or teaching, or a story, parable, vision or memory being told), draw what the words describe and leave the speaker, writer and listeners out, unless the text shows them inside that scene (a visionary within the vision). Never put a speaker, writer or listener into a scene their words only describe, and never make them a figure of their own words, such as the king ready for battle or the man standing in the gap.
- In `selectedCast`, list every section cast entry that will be visible: people, groups, places, objects, and any presence without form shown through its effects. Give a few words of the text for each. Leave out cast who are elsewhere or only mentioned. Anyone without a cast entry may appear as an unnamed role or crowd when the moment needs them.
- Describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Leave fixed appearance to canon, name no art style, and ask for no visible writing: scrolls, tablets, letters and books stay rolled or closed, and signs and boards are blank. Describe only what can be seen; leave out unseen or invisible beings, because anything named gets drawn. Keep every depiction rule.
- The scene fields carry this moment's place, time, light and situational clothing. The SECTION LOOK GUIDE is a suggestion for them: keep what fits this moment and change what does not. OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS, when given instead, are binding: keep the setting and time of day consistent with them.
- Each field is one or two short phrases.

Depiction rules:

- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.

You check an illustration plan before it is drawn. You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.
The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.
Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.
- outside_instant: a selected or described person or presence does not belong in this moment, such as a speaker, writer, prophet or listener put into a scene their words only describe or made a figure of their own words, the narrator of a story or vision, someone from a different event, or a no-form presence the moment does not show. Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.
- look_conflict: an OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS value (only when supplied) contradicts the scene, the text or the depiction rules. Quote that value.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts a selected entry's fixed canon. Quote the scene field.
- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.
For each problem, copy a short exact phrase from a scene field or a selected id into planQuote (from an owner constraint for look_conflict) and give a one-sentence reason.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Elisha son of Shaphat

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Elisha son of Shaphat: a man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and sun-browned from working the fields, lean and steady in build. Dark skin, a bald head, and a close-cut beard with some grey at the chin. Calm, weathered face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a cloak of rough brown wool. Signature prop: Elijah's mantle, a dark sheepskin cloak he wears over his shoulders.
- Bethel: a walled hill town on a rocky ridge of central Judah-Israel highland, terraced olive groves and terebinths on the slopes, low flat-roofed stone and mud-brick houses, a city gate of heavy timber and stone, and a raised high place with an altar of dressed stone and an Asherah pole beside it, with the golden-calf shrine as its central landmark.
- Mount Carmel: a long, rounded limestone ridge rising above the Mediterranean coast, its slopes covered with low scrub, oak, terebinth and wild flowers, bare rock outcrops at the crest, a broad flat summit suitable for an altar, and an old stone-built altar site among the rocks.
- Only Elisha son of Shaphat, Bethel (prophets' community and calf shrine in Kings), Mount Carmel have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Elisha, a solitary prophet in plain cloak, walking forward on the road with head bared
Action: A band of youths pours out of the city gate, mocking and gesturing toward Elisha as he climbs the road
Setting: Bethel, a hill town of stone houses at the city gate, with a rocky slope rising toward Mount Carmel in the distance
Secondary elements: Several youths in simple undyed tunics crowding near the gate, arms raised in jeering gestures; dust rising from the lane
Mood: Tense, contemptuous and disrespectful, with a sense of quiet dignity in the lone prophet
Time of day: Midday, bright and clear, dry and still hot air
Composition: Wide view from slightly below the road, Elisha small on the ascending path in the foreground, youths grouped at the gate in the background

ART STYLE: Ink & Watercolor
Rendering: Pen-and-ink drawing with transparent watercolor washes laid over the whole picture; a finished watercolor painting of the work's world, not a sketch.
Negatives: Washes, pigment and scenery must reach every edge. No white or cream paper margins, unpainted corners, paper edges, sketchbook, tape, border or vignette. Do not present the scene on a sheet of paper or against a blank backdrop. Avoid photorealism, digital airbrush smoothness and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Transparent washes of ochre, sienna, indigo and sage covering the whole picture, sky and corners included.
Lighting: Clear natural light; shadows as cool layered washes.
Materials and texture: Confident ink linework, wet-in-wet blooms and granulating pigment within the depicted world.
Composition: A complete scene: setting, sky and ground painted out to every edge and corner, with detail concentrated on key subjects.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- After: He looked behind him and saw them, and cursed them in Yahweh’s name. Then two female bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of those youths.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.
- Babylon: a vast walled city of baked brick on a flat plain watered by broad canals and rivers, its wide walls rising high and its great gates of bronze-banded cedar. Date palms and reed beds line the riverbanks, and ziggurat towers and palace roofs of brick rise above the flat skyline, with the temple of Bel among them.
- Only The Israelite people (the children of Israel), Babylon have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: A huddled group of exiled Israelites seated on the riverbank, heads lowered and shoulders bowed in grief.
Action: They sit down together and weep quietly by the water.
Setting: Reed-lined canal outside Babylon with a grassy bank, distant brick ziggurat and city walls on the horizon.
Secondary elements: Worn undyed wool cloaks and tunics, sand-stained; a few sheathed-quiet harps left resting on the ground beside them, unplayed; still water reflecting the fading sky.
Mood: Sorrowful, mournful stillness with quiet dignity.
Time of day: Dusk shifting to night; clear still air with low evening haze over the water; fading amber sunset light giving way to cool blue dusk and first stars.
Composition: Wide view from the far bank, the seated group in the lower foreground, the canal stretching across the middle, Babylon's walls and ziggurat small on the horizon.

Rendering: Pen-and-ink drawing with transparent watercolor washes laid over the whole picture; a finished watercolor painting of the work's world, not a sketch.
Negatives: Washes, pigment and scenery must reach every edge. No white or cream paper margins, unpainted corners, paper edges, sketchbook, tape, border or vignette. Do not present the scene on a sheet of paper or against a blank backdrop. Avoid photorealism, digital airbrush smoothness and cartoon caricature.

Lighting: Clear natural light; shadows as cool layered washes.
Materials and texture: Confident ink linework, wet-in-wet blooms and granulating pigment within the depicted world.
Composition: A complete scene: setting, sky and ground painted out to every edge and corner, with detail concentrated on key subjects.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- After: On the willows in that land, we hung up our harps.

- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Isaiah son of Amoz: a man in his fifties, lean and sinewy, with a weathered brown skin of the Judean hill country. Dark hair graying at the temples, worn to the shoulders, and a short, full grey beard. Deep-set, steady eyes and a long, lined face marked by years of hard counsel. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist and a rough brown wool cloak in earth tones. Carries a simple wooden staff, the sign of a traveling prophet.
- Seraphim: a heavenly being of tall, luminous human-like form, ageless, with burnished bronze-gold skin. Six wings: two cover the face, two cover the feet, two lift in flight, feathered in white and gold. Face hidden behind the wings. Robed in a long linen tunic of pale white. Carries a glowing live coal held in long iron tongs, the coal burning orange-red.
- Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.
- Only Isaiah son of Amoz, Seraphim, Yahweh's house in Jerusalem (the temple) have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

Setting: A high cedar and stone hall of the Jerusalem temple with a raised sanctuary.
Secondary elements: Incense smoke and glowing cloud spread between the pillars, with fire and radiance filling the hall from the Lord's presence, which stays unseen.
Mood: Awe, reverence and trembling stillness.
Time of day: Early morning in first light, air still and heavy with incense and dust.
Composition: Low viewpoint looking up at Isaiah, with the seraphim arching above him and the sanctuary glowing behind.

ART STYLE: Byzantine Icon
Rendering: Byzantine icon painting: flat, frontal, stylized figures with elongated proportions, solemn timeless expressions, inverse perspective and symbolic rather than naturalistic space.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor.

Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Daniel (prophet of Babylon)

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Daniel: a lean, dignified Judean man in his youth grown to a grave, graying elder; olive-brown skin; dark hair cropped close and a short trimmed beard flecked with grey; deep-set, steady eyes and a calm, thoughtful face. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a plain indigo wool cloak with a blue fringed hem. Props: a small leather scroll case slung at the hip.
- Babylon: a vast walled city of baked brick on a flat plain watered by broad canals and rivers, its wide walls rising high and its great gates of bronze-banded cedar. Date palms and reed beds line the riverbanks, and ziggurat towers and palace roofs of brick rise above the flat skyline, with the temple of Bel among them.

Rendering: Byzantine icon painting: flat, frontal, stylized figures with elongated proportions, solemn timeless expressions, inverse perspective and symbolic rather than naturalistic space.

You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.

- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church. People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule. Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing. Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.

- The beloved disciple: a young man of about thirty, lean and quick, with a sun-browned skin of the Galilean fishing shore. Dark brown hair cut just above the ears, a short, close beard, and a calm, steady, attentive face with deep-set eyes. He wears a plain undyed linen tunic of ochre-brown under a dark wool cloak of earth brown. He carries a simple wooden walking staff.
- Sea of Galilee: a large freshwater lake set in hilly terrain of basalt and limestone, its shores sloping to pebbled and sandy beaches. Low stone-built fishing villages and wooden fishing boats line the water, with nets drying on the shore. Reeds, oleanders and palms grow along the banks, and fig and olive trees climb the hills above.
- The Twelve Disciples: men of about twenty to forty years; sun-browned, lean and sturdy from fishing and walking; olive to weathered brown skin; short or shoulder-length dark hair and close-trimmed beards; plain, earnest faces. You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.
Cast marked hasForm: false have no body and are never drawn. Describe only the shared place, weather and light. Where the section shows one of them, its presence may appear only as smoke, cloud, fire, wind or light spread through the place. Never describe its throne, seat, chariot, robe, train, face, hands, hair, body or silhouette, even as an empty seat, a denial or a figure made of light: bodily words in the text are metaphors. Keep formed characters' own situational clothing and props attached to them. The cast list covers the whole section; do not force every cast member into the shared setting or add individual poses, actions or moments.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Visionary heaven and renewal. People: Seers, heavenly beings and the redeemed as described. Dress: Robes and garments with the text's colors and materials. Buildings and objects: Thrones, altars, glass-like sea and jeweled city as described.

STORY SECTION: New heaven and new earth

I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth have passed away, and the sea is no more.

PRIORITY RULES:
1) No text or symbols anywhere: no letters, numbers, signage, logos or inscriptions, no writing on scrolls, tablets, books, boards or halos, and no artist's signature or initials in a corner.
2) One scene painted to every edge of the frame: no panels, collage, border, frame, margin, visible paper or blank backdrop, and never a photographed painting or mockup.
3) Nothing from outside the moment's era.
4) Natural anatomy: no extra or malformed limbs, hands or faces.
5) sexually explicit content and lingering gore are never shown; serious depictions of battles, blood, death and crucifixion and non-sexual nudity may be, treated seriously.
6) No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.
7) Show the SELECTED CHARACTERS with their canon. Anyone else appears only as an unnamed figure the scene plan describes.
8) A subject without form is never drawn. Only when it is selected may the light, cloud, smoke, fire or wind in the scene plan stand for it, with nobody in them. A throne or seat stays empty unless the scene plan names who sits on it.
If instructions conflict, follow these rules, then the work brief, then canon, then the art style, then the scene plan. The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.

SCENE: one moment of The Holy Bible, Matthew 27:35: "When they had crucified him, they divided his clothing among them, casting lots,"

WORK BRIEF (bible-web; what may be shown; it outranks the style, the look and the plan):
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction: God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
Depiction: Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
Depiction: No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
Depiction: Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
Depiction: Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Roman Judea and the early church
People: Jewish and Gentile Mediterranean communities under Roman rule.
Dress: Tunics, cloaks, priestly robes and Roman military clothing.
Buildings and objects: Stone villages, synagogues, temple, fishing boats and Roman cities.
Technology: Oil lamps, sail and oar, roads, coins and papyrus; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: The Roman soldiers; Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- The Roman soldiers: adult men, late twenties to forties; sturdy, disciplined build; olive to tan skin of Mediterranean men; short-cropped dark or brown hair, clean-shaven or close-cropped beard; stern, weathered faces. Signature dress: a short tunic of undyed linen under a red-brown woollen military cloak, leather belt and sandals, bronze helmet worn at the cohort. Props: a short sword at the hip and a tall rectangular shield.
- Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.
- Golgotha: a rounded rocky knoll of pale limestone rising just outside the walls of Jerusalem, bare of trees and scrub except for thin dry grass in cracks. Its crown is worn smooth and bony-white, giving the hill its name, the place of a skull. A rough stone-cut quarry face and a few low olive trees stand at its foot, and the walls and towers of the city rise distant behind it.
- Only The Roman soldiers, Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord, Golgotha have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Soldiers in military tunics and leather armor, kneeling and bent over cloth and dice-like lots on the ground.
Action: Soldiers divide garments and cast lots at the base of the cross.
Setting: Golgotha, a bare rocky hill outside Jerusalem with stone walls far in the distance.
Secondary elements: Crosses rising behind, Jesus hanging above with head bowed, a few distant onlookers in plain tunics and cloaks.
Mood: Sombre, restrained, quietly grave.
Time of day: Midday light turning dim, hot still air, sky beginning to darken.
Composition: Low viewpoint from the hillside, soldiers in the foreground, crosses and the figure of Jesus rising in the background.

ART STYLE: Byzantine Icon
Rendering: Byzantine icon painting: flat, frontal, stylized figures with elongated proportions, solemn timeless expressions, inverse perspective and symbolic rather than naturalistic space.
Negatives: Never show a wooden panel, panel edges, frame, border, wall or the icon as a physical object. Avoid photorealism and modern illustration. The gold sky and stylized landscape fill the image edge-to-edge.
Palette: Burnished gold-leaf sky, deep reds, ultramarine, ochres and earth greens.
Lighting: No cast shadows; inner light shown through layered highlights and gold glow.
Materials and texture: Egg tempera and gold-leaf texture within the scene.
Composition: Hieratic, balanced staging; the key subject largest and central; stylized rocks, buildings and trees.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject, landscape and layout.
- Image 2: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

NARRATIVE CONTINUITY (cues only; compose the current moment):
- Before: they gave him sour wine to drink mixed with gall. When he had tasted it, he would not drink.
- After: and they sat and watched him there.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.

Technology: Ancient lamps, trumpets, harps, swords and sailing ships; no modern objects.

SELECTED CHARACTERS: Four living creatures (Revelation)

UNSEEN PRESENCE (binding): the light, cloud, smoke, fire and wind in the scene plan are light and weather spread through the place, not one glowing shape. Nobody stands, sits or hovers in them.

CANON (fixed identity of the figures, places and things present; the scene plan decides pose, expression and action):
- Four living creatures: ageless and powerful, each with six wings set close about the body; the wings and bodies are covered with eyes, around and within. One is lion-like with a mane of tawny gold, one calf-like with a sleek red-brown hide, one with a human face of grave dignity and dark skin, one eagle-like with bronze-gold feathers. Robes of deep crimson and white.
- Heavenly throne room: a vast open sanctuary of radiance beneath a heaven like crystal, floored with a sea of glass that is clear as crystal, set with a great throne and a temple whose doors open onto the heavens, lit by lightnings, thunders and a rainbow the colour of emerald about the throne. Pale gold and white stone, jasper and sardius glimmer in the walls; an altar of gold stands before the throne.
- Only Four living creatures (Revelation), Heavenly throne room have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Four strange winged living creatures standing close around a central throne, their many eyes gleaming.
Action: They stand still in quiet watchful attendance, facing outward with eyes open on every side.
Setting: A vast heavenly hall with a clear sea of glass spread before the throne, smooth and crystalline.
Secondary elements: Faint luminous mist rising over the glassy sea, jeweled glow reflecting off its surface, radiant light spreading from beyond the frame where the throne presence is felt but not shown.
Mood: Awe-filled, still and reverent.
Time of day: Timeless heavenly light, clear and unchanging, with no storm.
Composition: Wide view from before the throne, the creatures arranged around the center, the glassy sea stretching in the foreground to the radiant distance.

ART STYLE: Ink & Watercolor
Rendering: Pen-and-ink drawing with transparent watercolor washes laid over the whole picture; a finished watercolor painting of the work's world, not a sketch.
Negatives: Washes, pigment and scenery must reach every edge. No white or cream paper margins, unpainted corners, paper edges, sketchbook, tape, border or vignette. Do not present the scene on a sheet of paper or against a blank backdrop. Avoid photorealism, digital airbrush smoothness and cartoon caricature.
Palette: Transparent washes of ochre, sienna, indigo and sage covering the whole picture, sky and corners included.
Lighting: Clear natural light; shadows as cool layered washes.
Materials and texture: Confident ink linework, wet-in-wet blooms and granulating pigment within the depicted world.
Composition: A complete scene: setting, sky and ground painted out to every edge and corner, with detail concentrated on key subjects.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges and corners.
